A FEW USEFUL COORDINATES

The science behind the view.

Perigee combines two NASA/JPL sources: a catalog of predicted Earth close approaches, and precise positions for each object over time. It's an educational explorer, not a NASA product or an impact-warning tool.

What you're looking at

  • Table, timeline and stats list each asteroid's predicted closest approach in the 30-day window, from NASA NeoWs. A row is an event, not the object's current location.
  • 3D view shows where objects are at the displayed UTC time, using Earth-centered positions from JPL Horizons. Only objects inside the chosen viewing radius (25, 50 or 100 lunar distances) appear.
  • Selected path is the object's predicted next 30 days relative to Earth. It's a flyby track, not an orbit around Earth, and has no uncertainty envelope.
  • 2D schematic is illustrative: directions are decorative and distances use a log scale.

Scale and markers

  • Distances and the Earth, Moon and Sun share one true linear scale. When Earth or the Moon is too small to see, a ring and label mark where it is.
  • Asteroid dots are enlarged so they stay visible. Their size follows NASA's estimated diameter on a compressed scale; hollow means unknown.
  • 1 lunar distance (LD) ≈ 384,400 km. The blue Moon line and amber Earth-orbit line are reference ellipses that slowly change over time.

Using the controls

  • Drag to rotate. Click the view first, then scroll or pinch to zoom. Arrow keys, +/− and Home also work.
  • The time slider and Play move every position together. Live clock follows the current time; Now returns to it.
  • Select a dot or table row for details and its path. Select the Moon or Sun for their profiles.

Classification and imagery

"Potentially hazardous" (PHA) is NASA's classification based on orbit and size. It is not an impact probability; see NASA's definition and Sentry impact monitoring. Confirmed images come from a small reviewed list; other image matches from NASA's archive are labeled unverified. All imagery is historical, not a live camera.

Freshness

Waiting for the data source.

The catalog refreshes every 15 minutes while Live clock is on. Positions are cached for an hour. If NASA is unavailable, a dated saved snapshot is shown and labeled. Earth imagery: NASA Blue Marble (Reto Stöckli) and night lights (NASA Earth Observatory / Suomi NPP VIIRS). Moon: NASA SVS / LRO. Blue Marble source · Night-light source
